reason: The applicant meets all the requirements of § 14 (1) as an Estonian citizen with secondary education, full legal capacity, and required Estonian language skills. Furthermore, none of the prohibitions in § 15 apply, as the applicant has no criminal conviction and no family conflict with a supervising official.
The applicant has a conviction for an intentional crime, which disqualifies them from being hired into the civil service under § 15 point 1.
The right of withdrawal does not apply because the subject of the contract falls into an excluded category under § 53 (4) (custom-made according to the consumer's personal needs).

To determine if the consumer can withdraw from the distance contract, it must be established whether the 14-day withdrawal period is still running or if a withdrawal notice was already sent within that timeframe.

The applicant meets all statutory requirements for the supplementary tax exemption: they own residential land where their primary residence is registered, they receive a state pension, the municipality has established the exemption, and the required application has been submitted.
To receive the supplementary tax exemption, the local municipality council must have established the exemption. It is currently unknown whether the municipality has set this exemption.

The statute explicitly states that the disclosure of personal data must not excessively harm the rights of the data subject. Since the publication would excessively harm the subject, the processing is forbidden.

The statute permits processing personal data without consent for journalistic purposes if there is public interest, it aligns with journalism ethics, and it does not excessively harm the data subject. The facts confirm all these conditions are met.

The building project conforms to the detailed plan, meets building requirements, was prepared by a competent designer, and includes the required site study, satisfying the conditions for granting a building permit without triggering any refusal grounds.

The project conforms to the detailed plan and building requirements, was prepared by a competent designer, and includes the required site study, satisfying all statutory requirements for a building permit.

Under § 120(3) of the Family Law Act, if making a joint declaration would cause a delay contrary to the child's interests, one parent has the right to make necessary decisions alone in the interests of the child.

Under § 120(3) of the Family Law Act, a parent who shares joint custody and does not have delegated decision rights may act alone only if waiting for joint consent would cause a delay contrary to the child's interests (an emergency). Since it is unknown whether there is an emergency, more information is needed.

The applicant is an Estonian citizen with the required education, legal capacity, and Estonian-language proficiency. The known facts show no disqualifying intentional-crime conviction or supervisory family conflict.
Although the applicant meets the general requirements in § 14(1), § 15(1) prohibits appointment because the applicant has a current conviction for an intentionally committed crime.

The contract concerns a custom-made item tailored to the consumer’s personal needs, which falls within a § 53(4) excluded category. Therefore, the § 56(1) 14-day right of withdrawal does not apply, despite timely notice.
The contract is covered by the withdrawal right and no exclusion applies, but it is unknown whether the withdrawal period is still running or a withdrawal notice was sent within that period.
The applicant owns residential land where their registered residence is located, receives a state pension, the municipality has established the exemption, and the required application was submitted.
The applicant satisfies the statutory land, residence, pensioner, and application conditions, but the supplementary exemption exists only if the municipal council has established it.

Kuigi töötlemisel on ajakirjanduslik eesmärk, avalik huvi ja kooskõla ajakirjanduseetikaga, ei tohi avalikustamine ülemäära kahjustada andmesubjekti õigusi. Teadaolevalt põhjustaks avaldamine ülemäärast kahju.

The consent-free exception requires a journalistic purpose. Public interest, compliance with journalism ethics, and absence of excessive harm are established; consent is not required under this exception.
The project conforms to the detailed plan and building requirements, was prepared by a competent person, and is supported by the required site study. No stated refusal ground applies.

Projekt vastab detailplaneeringule ja ehitusnõuetele, selle koostas pädev isik ning nõutav ehitusuuring on olemas. Ükski § 44 loetletud keeldumise alus ei esine; riigilõivu tasumine ei ole toodud sätetes ehitusloa andmise sisuline tingimus.

Under § 120(3), one parent may act alone when obtaining both parents’ joint decision would cause delay contrary to the child’s interests. The hospital emergency and the other parent’s unavailability satisfy that condition; the other parent must be notified without delay.

The mother lacks sole custody, delegated decision-making authority, and the other parent’s consent. Acting alone may nevertheless be permitted if urgent action is necessary to avoid delay contrary to the child’s interests, so whether there is an emergency is required.

Applicant meets all § 14(1) requirements (Estonian citizen, secondary education, Estonian language proficiency, full legal capacity) and no § 15 exclusion applies: no conviction for an intentional crime and no declared family conflict with a supervising official.

Under § 15 p 1, a person with an unexpunged conviction (karistatus) for an intentionally committed crime may not be taken into service. The applicant has such a conviction still on record, so despite meeting § 14(1) requirements, employment is forbidden.

The item is custom-made to the consumer's personal needs, falling under § 53 lg 4 p 2 excluded category, so the § 56 lg 1 withdrawal right does not apply despite the 14-day period still running and timely notice.

Consumer and distance contract requirements are met and no § 53 lg 4 exclusion applies, but withdrawal under § 56 requires the 14-day period to be running or a timely withdrawal notice to have been sent (§ 56 lg 1, 2^1). Both facts are unknown.

All statutory conditions are met: the land is elamumaa owned by the applicant with registered residence there (§11(1^1)), the municipality has set the exemption, the applicant receives a state pension (§11(5)(1)), and the application was submitted per §11(7). The supplementary exemption is permitted.

Under § 11(1) and (5), the exemption applies only if the municipal council has established it by regulation by 1 October of the preceding year. All personal conditions (owner, residential land, registered residence, pensioner, application) are met, but whether the municipality has set the exemption is unknown and is decisive.

Although the processing is journalistic, in the public interest, and consistent with ethics, the statute forbids disclosure that excessively harms the data subject's rights. Excessive harm is established, so publication without consent is not permitted.

The statute permits processing without consent only if it is for a journalistic purpose, with public interest, ethics compliance, and no excessive harm. Public interest, ethics, and lack of excessive harm are established, and consent is unnecessary under this provision, but the journalistic purpose claim is not yet verified in the known facts.

The project conforms to the detailed plan and building requirements (§ 42(1)), was prepared by a competent person, is based on a site study, and no ground for refusal under § 44 applies. The permit must be granted.

The project conforms to the detailed plan and building requirements (§ 42(1)), and no refusal ground under § 44 applies: a competent designer prepared the project, the site study is available, and there is no plan violation. The state fee is not a statutory condition here (and was stated as paid anyway).

Under Perekonnaseadus § 120(3), where obtaining a joint declaration of will from both parents would cause a delay contrary to the child's interests, one parent may make the necessary decisions and acts alone in the child's interests. Here the applicant is a parent, there is a medical emergency, and the other parent is unreachable, so the mother may decide alone; she must notify the other parent without delay afterwards.

Under PKS § 118 lg 1 parents with joint custody must act jointly; the applicant lacks sole custody (§ 120 lg 2 p 1), no delegated decision right (§ 119), and no consent from the other parent (§ 120 lg 7 presumption is rebutted). The only remaining basis to act alone is § 120 lg 3, which permits a parent to act alone if joint action would cause a delay contrary to the child's interests (an emergency). Whether an emergency exists is unknown, so the case cannot be decided.

The applicant is an Estonian citizen with at least secondary education, full legal capacity, and required Estonian language proficiency, satisfying § 14(1). No disqualifying conditions under § 15 are present: no criminal conviction, no family conflict, and no other listed bars.
The applicant has a criminal conviction for an intentional crime, which is a disqualifying condition under § 15(1)1.
The contract concerns a custom-made item tailored to the consumer's personal needs, which falls under § 53 lg 4 p 2, excluding the right of withdrawal under § 56 lg 1.
The right to withdraw under § 56(1) requires that the 14-day period is still running and that a timely notice has been sent. These facts are unknown.

The applicant is the owner of residential land with registered primary residence, receives a state pension, the municipality has set the exemption, and the application has been submitted. All statutory conditions for the supplementary pensioner exemption are met.

The statute requires the local municipality to have established the exemption by regulation before the tax period. Without knowing whether the municipality has set the exemption, the request cannot be decided.

The statute permits processing without consent only if there is public interest, it is consistent with journalism ethics, and it does not excessively harm the data subject's rights. Here, excessive_harm is true, so the condition is not met.
The statute permits processing without consent for journalistic purposes if there is public interest, compliance with journalism ethics, and no excessive harm. Known facts satisfy these conditions.
The project conforms to the detailed plan, meets building requirements, was prepared by a competent designer, and a site study has been provided. No grounds for refusal under § 44 are present.

The project conforms to the detailed plan, meets building requirements, was prepared by a competent designer, and a site study is provided. No grounds for refusal under § 44 are present. The unpaid fee is not a listed ground for refusal.

Under § 120(3), when a joint parental decision would cause a delay contrary to the child's interests, one parent may act alone in the child's interests. The child is in hospital, the other parent is unreachable, and an emergency exists, so the mother may make the necessary decision alone.

The applicant is a parent without sole custody or delegated decision right, and both parents' consent is not confirmed. Under § 120(3), a parent may act alone only in an emergency causing delay contrary to the child's interests. Since the emergency fact is unknown, the decision cannot be made.
